claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) A diagnosis of exclusion: the secondary causes of sinus tachycardia must be ruled out first

claims.text: Mechanism: unknown; proposed components are increased sinus node automaticity, decreased vagal sensitivity and increased beta-adrenergic sensitivity
claims.quote: The etiology of the syndrome of inappropriate sinus tachycardia is unknown. Potential components include Increased intrinsic sinus node automaticity Decreased vagal sensitivity Augmented beta-adrenergic sensitivity

claims.text: Who: mainly females, from the late second to the mid fourth decade of life
claims.quote: Syndrome of inappropriate sinus tachycardia mainly affects females in their late second decade to mid fourth decade

claims.text: Symptoms Very symptomatic: palpitations, orthostatic and exercise intolerance, weakness, fatigue, dyspnea, chest discomfort, anxiety
claims.quote: Typically, patients with the syndrome of inappropriate sinus tachycardia are very symptomatic with palpitations, orthostatic intolerance, exercise intolerance, weakness, fatigue, dyspnea, chest discomfort, and anxiety.

claims.text: Tachycardia worsens on standing without orthostatic hypotension (this separates it from POTS)
claims.quote: Physical findings are those of tachycardia aggravated by standing in the absence of orthostatic hypotension. The latter helps to distinguish the syndrome from postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).

claims.text: Physical activity (down-regulates beta-adrenergic activity); yoga, meditation or breathing exercises (up-regulate vagal activity)
claims.quote: Down-regulation of beta-adrenergic activity through physical activity Up-regulation of vagal activity (eg, with yoga, meditation, breathing exercises)

claims.text: Beta blocker or non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker
